title: OpenAI raised bug-bounty payouts. A critical ChatGPT finding can now reach $30,000
friendlyTitle: OpenAI raised payments for security bug reports. A serious ChatGPT flaw can now reach $30,000
summary: On 2 November, OpenAI said it is more than quadrupling the midpoint of its reward ranges for medium, high, and critical findings, on average. A critical vulnerability in a core product, which it names as ChatGPT, Codex, or the API platform, can now earn up to $30,000. Exceptional critical findings on those targets remain eligible for up to $100,000, and up to $172,000 with bonuses. OpenAI's example of that top case, with a quality bonus, a priority-campaign bonus, and a loyalty bonus, comes to $171,925. The examples are illustrative. Reports not yet awarded get the new ranges. Awards made in the 30 days before the announcement get the difference if the new ranges would have paid more, on the base award plus loyalty. The programme page is on Bugcrowd.

whyItMatters: This is a payment change for people who already report flaws, not a new lock on your account. If you sent a report in the last month and it has not been paid, the new range is the one to check. A higher bounty is also a signal that OpenAI expects serious findings in ChatGPT, Codex, and the API, not a promise that those products are now safer.
